Inamul Haq Alias Aman
--Applicant
 Versus

--Respondent
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Vikas Singh, learned counsel for 
the applicant.
2. Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned Additional 
Advocate General along with Mr. S.C. Dumka, 
learned A.G.A. and Mr. Nikhil Bisht, learned 
Brief Holder for the State.
3. By means of the present application, 
the applicant seeks anticipatory bail in 
connection with Case Crime/F.I.R. No. 
0163 of 2026, registered at Police Station 
Vikas Nagar, District Dehradun, for the 
offences punishable under Sections 351(2) 
and 69 of the B.N.S.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant 
would submit that the applicant has falsely 
been implicated in the present case on the 
basis of wholly unfounded and fabricated 
allegations; that, the impugned F.I.R. does 
not disclose any specific date, time or 
particular occasion on which the applicant 
allegedly committed the offence of sexual  intercourse with the complainant; that, the 
applicant is presently pursuing his M.Tech. 
course at a University in Italy and, 
therefore, is presently residing there for the 
purpose of his studies.
5. He would further submit that the 
applicant is ready and willing to return to 
India and undertakes to cooperate with the 
investigation as and when required by the 
Investigating Officer, however, some 
reasonable time is required by him to 
complete the necessary formalities and 
arrangements for returning to India. 
Learned counsel, therefore, submits that, 
in the circumstances, the applicant may be 
granted interim protection from arrest for a 
period of four weeks so as to enable him to 
return to India and participate in the 
investigation.
6. Learned State Counsel would 
vehemently oppose the prayer for 
anticipatory bail. However, on the basis of 
instructions received, he does not dispute 
the fact that the applicant is presently 
pursuing his M.Tech. course in Italy and 
that some time would be required by him 
to complete the necessary formalities for 
his return to India. Learned State Counsel, 
however, submits that the applicant may 
be directed to cooperate with the 
investigation and to remain available 
before the Investigating Officer as and 
when required.
7. Having considered the submissions 
advanced by learned counsel for the 
parties and taking into consideration the  nature of the allegations, the contents of 
the F.I.R. and the fact that the applicant is 
presently pursuing his M.Tech. course in 
Italy, this Court is of the prima facie view 
that the applicant has made out a case for 
grant of limited interim protection from 
arrest. At the same time, it is made clear 
that the observations contained herein are 
confined only to the consideration of the 
prayer for interim protection and shall not 
be construed as an expression of opinion 
on the merits of the case.
8. List this case on 27.10.2026.
9. Having considered the submissions 
advanced by the learned counsel for the 
parties, the nature of the allegations, the 
material available on record, this Court is 
of the prima facie view that the applicant 
has made out a case for grant of interim 
anticipatory bail till the next date of listing.
10. Accordingly, it is directed that the 
investigation shall proceed independently, 
fairly and strictly in accordance with law 
and shall not be influenced by any 
observation made in this order. However, 
in the event of arrest of the applicant in 
connection with the aforesaid Case 
Crime/F.I.R., he shall be released on 
interim anticipatory bail till the next date 
of listing on his furnishing a personal bond 
along with two reliable sureties, each in 
the like amount, to the satisfaction of the 
Arresting Officer/Investigating Officer, 
subject to the following conditions:
(i) The applicant shall cooperate with the 
investigation and shall appear before the  Investigating Officer as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or 
indirectly make any inducement, threat or 
promise to any person acquainted with the 
facts of the case so as to dissuade such 
person from disclosing such facts to the 
Court or to the Investigating Agency;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave the territory 
of India without prior permission of the Court 
concerned;
(iv) The applicant shall not misuse the liberty 
granted by this order and shall maintain 
peace and good conduct during the period of 
interim protection;
(v) In case of breach of any of the aforesaid 
conditions, it shall be open to the 
State/prosecution to seek modification or 
cancellation of interim anticipatory bail in 
accordance with law.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 11.08.2026 Mamta

Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav, Advocate for the 
applicant.
Mr. Rakesh Kumar Joshi, A.G.A. and Mr. Manoj 
Bhatt, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
2. The applicant has moved the present 
Miscellaneous Application (I.A. No.1 of 2026) seeking 
permission to travel to Messina, Italy, where he is 
pursuing his M.Tech. course in Engineering.
3. Learned State Counsel was directed to obtain 
instructions in the matter. Today, on instructions, 
learned State Counsel submits that charge-sheet has 
already been filed in the matter on 20.08.2026. He 
further submits that, at present, the personal 
presence of the applicant before the learned trial 
Court is not required and, if this Court deems it 
appropriate, the applicant may be permitted to travel 
to Messina, Italy for pursuing his higher studies.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and 
perused the record. It is not disputed that the 
applicant was pursuing his M.Tech. course even prior 
to the lodging of the F.I.R. It is also stated that the 
applicant has cooperated with the investigation and 
has appeared before the Investigating Officer as and 
when required. The applicant has further stated in 
the application that his parents are permanent 
residents of Dehradun and own property there. He 
has undertaken that, as and when his presence is 
required by the learned trial Court, he shall appear  before the Court and shall not seek any unnecessary 
adjournment or otherwise cause delay in the 
proceedings.
5. Having regard to the aforesaid facts and 
circumstances, particularly the fact that the charge￾sheet has already been filed, the applicant has 
cooperated with the investigation, and his higher 
studies are being pursued at Messina, Italy, this 
Court is of the view that the applicant may be 
permitted to travel abroad for the aforesaid purpose. 
The permission, however, shall remain subject to his 
furnishing adequate security and undertaking to 
ensure his appearance before the learned trial Court 
as and when required.
6. Accordingly, the applicant is permitted to travel 
to Messina, Italy for pursuing his M.Tech. 
course/higher studies, subject to the following 
conditions:
(i) The applicant shall furnish two reliable sureties to 
the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
(ii) The applicant shall furnish an undertaking before 
the learned trial Court that he shall appear before the 
Court as and when his personal presence is 
specifically required.
(iii) The applicant shall cooperate with the trial and 
shall not, either directly or indirectly, cause any 
unnecessary delay in the conclusion of the 
proceedings.
(iv) The applicant shall furnish his complete address, 
contact details and details of his course/institution in 
Italy before the learned trial Court and shall keep the 
Court informed of any change therein; and
(v) The applicant shall return to India and appear 
before the learned trial Court whenever so directed.
7. Subject to the aforesaid conditions, the present 
Miscellaneous Application (I.A. No.1 of 2026) stands 
disposed of.
8. List in due course.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 
 16.09.2026
Arpan
